dedupe_keys.name: global high resolution mining footprints tang and werner 74 548 polygons

description: This global mining land use dataset outlines mine features mapped from high-resolution, publicly available satellite imagery: 74,548 polygons covering about 66,000 square kilometres of waste rock dumps, pits, water ponds, tailings dams, heap leach pads and processing and milling infrastructure. The DataCite record says the polygons follow the edges of each feature and leave out the land between them, so they separate mine feature categories, not drawing broad mining areas. The creators are given as Liang Tang and Tim T. Werner (2023), and this copy was released as version 1.0 on 10 April 2025 on the Climateverse India Dataverse, open access and free under CC0 1.0, with global coverage. Caveats: the download format, the imagery dates and the list of mines are not stated on the page read, and this is a mirror, so the original publication should be checked for updates. For simulation it gives detailed polygons of tailings dams, pits and processing plants to expose mine assets to floods, landslides and earthquakes, and to seed dam failure and pollution scenarios downstream. Related catalogue records include the global-scale mining polygons by Maus and others, the global copper mining areas 2022 and the Mapping Mining Areas in the Tropics dataset.
